content:
In August this year, Fender launched the MIX wireless headphones, priced at US$299. These over-ear headphones feature replaceable batteries and the FWD Tx USB-C wireless transmitter, delivering low-latency, lossless connection quality. Fender MIX headphones can now also be tuned via an iPhone app, allowing users to adjust their listening experience to suit their preferences.

The Fender Audio iPhone app offers EQ presets and a customisable five-band equaliser, allowing independent adjustment of the bass, low-mid, mid, high-mid and treble frequency bands, so users can fine-tune the sound directly within the iPhone app to their liking.

The app also includes a battery display and customisable home screen widgets for quick access to features like EQ settings.

As for the headphones themselves, the MIX uses 40mm graphene drivers, hybrid active noise cancellation, and Bluetooth 5.3. Fender says battery life is up to 52 hours with ANC on, and up to 100 hours with ANC off.

The included USB-C transmitter supports multiple modes, including lossless audio up to 24-bit/96kHz, low-latency listening, and Auracast broadcasting to multiple compatible devices.

The headphones can also be used wired via USB-C or a 3.5mm audio cable.

After an initial listen, I found the MIX delivers a fairly solid sound with active noise cancellation on. However, when switching to Fender's transparency mode (ambient sound), the audio quality noticeably drops for my ears—at least when connected via Bluetooth without using the transmitter.

I'm looking forward to trying out the app's EQ controls so I can tune the sound closer to my personal taste.

When not in use, the USB-C transmitter can be stored behind the ear cup; if convenience matters more than sound quality, you can also simply connect via Bluetooth.

The Fender Audio app is now available on the App Store, supporting Fender MIX headphones.
